title: Precedence Tables and Expression Trees
description: Fold a flat infix token list under two precedence tables (standard vs. flat) to see how precedence numbers reshape the AST and change the result.
source: draft: agy free model + edit: codex

steps.description: Define PREC_STANDARD where '*' and '/' have precedence 2 while '+' and '-' have 1, alongside PREC_FLAT where all four operators have precedence 1.

In fold_left(tokens, prec_table), split tokens into nums and ops, then iterate over precedence levels from highest to lowest, replacing adjacent operands and their operator with a tuple (op, result_nums[i], result_nums[i+1]).

steps.question: When fold_left runs on ['2', '+', '3', '*', '4'] with PREC_STANDARD vs. PREC_FLAT, which operator gets folded first in each case?
steps.answer: With PREC_STANDARD, current_prec starts at 2 so '*' folds 3 and 4 first into ('*', 3.0, 4.0). With PREC_FLAT, all operators have precedence 1. The left-to-right scan folds '+' on 2 and 3 first into ('+', 2.0, 3.0).

steps.description: Define evaluate(node) to recursively compute the numeric value of a nested tuple tree and show(label, prec, tokens) to print both the tree and its value.
Compare PREC_STANDARD and PREC_FLAT on ['2', '+', '3', '*', '4'] and test left-associativity on ['6', '-', '2', '-', '1'].
Watch fold_left construct ('*', 3.0, 4.0) first during the current_prec == 2 pass under PREC_STANDARD.
